name: 18 (2026-11-25 morning)
what: core: source session on outputs that survive a restart and the horizon finder (Fable); Track A: fresh verifier for C18; Track E: independent review of the G3 scope
note: Releases core-v0.4 to v0.7 are on main; main also holds core's script changes of 2026-11-25 (the queue marker is removed from every job's environment). Rulings: coord/DECISIONS/0037 to 0039. The cards are preempted often by another partition: a run may take a day to get its hour; never wait for one. Read what the task needs, not everything; every number with its run id; prediction before every test; figures made by registered scripts and looked at.

items.task: Source session for the next release (core-v0.8), about two hours. Read tracks/core/NEXT_SOURCE.md first (written by the core lead on 2026-11-25: it names the files, lines, tests and references) and work in its order; close what you start, and if time runs short stop after item 1 and say so. (1) Outputs that survive a restart: (a) the tracker file is appended when the mesh starts from a restart file, header only on a fresh start (Track F's gate G1 waits for this: its vacuum passage runs as a chain that preemptions cut many times); (b) the mesh history files get their header once; (c) the record of <base>.cons.hst that is lost when the restart file was written one or two cycles before the record is due. These change the outputs of continued runs without an option: list them in the changelog as changes without an option. (2) Horizon finder: a stopping rule on the residual or a fixed number of polishing iterations after the mass rule is met, off by default; <particles> ah_exc_max_growth (default 4: nothing changes) or a guard relative to the last accepted radius (Track D's gate G2; Track A reads horizon masses to 1e-4). With it the interface lines D asks for. (3) python/nrpic/figstyle.py: PDFs without a creation date (and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH honoured); the vendored copy in harness/style/ is the orchestrator's: send the same change as a proposal (outbox). Tests as NEXT_SOURCE names them, predictions first, on processors; without the new options every run is byte-identical (byte regression against .work/build_cpu_v07, 75 items). Card build, and ONE card check through the shared queue at priority 2. Publish the executables under a NEW directory scratch/core/exe/<branch>/ with COMMIT, SHA256SUMS and READY (never replace a published one). Interface text as proposals under tracks/core/interfaces/. Tell F and D (outbox) which executable serves their runs and what changes for them.

items.title: fresh verifier for checklist item C18 of gate G2 (conv_ball and threshold_ball numbers)
items.task: Fresh verifier for item C18 of gate G2 of this track (decision 0016 item 4; coord/DECISIONS/0039 item 2). About ninety minutes, processors only, no card run. Trust nothing and do not read the lead's verdicts first (the outcome entries of threshold_ball/JOURNAL.md and conv_ball/JOURNAL.md, stage/REVIEW-wave3.md, stage/G2/CHECKLIST.md): take the claims from the result tables of threshold_ball/README.md and conv_ball/README.md (numbers with run ids), the criteria from scope/SCOPE.md, and the predictions as they were written before the runs (git log shows when). With readers of your own, not the package's scripts, recompute from the registered outputs: conv_ball A-20261121-120257-a2eb839 (horizon times and masses against mesh and particle number, the orders of convergence); threshold_ball A-20261124-131120-5c974ce, A-20261125-115027-17b419e, A-20261125-115550-fe60ff1 (which members form a horizon by the rule fixed in entry 1; detection times against the exact collapse time of the dust ball from a reference of your own; horizon masses; the bracket of the threshold; the ratio of the Hamiltonian constraint to 16 pi E outside the horizon). Test each reader on an analytic field first. A prediction before each recomputation, the outcome after it. Per claim: reproduced (to how many digits), not reproduced, or not checkable and why; criteria that failed as written are stated as failed (C3; the mesh-C half of T4). Figures you look at. Write stage/G2/VERIFIER-C18.md; only after it is written, a last section that compares with the lead's verdicts.

items.title: independent review of the scope of gate G3 before its runs
items.task: Independent review of the scope of gate G3 of this track BEFORE its production runs (scope/SCOPE.md section 4d, commit cbe20398; coord/DECISIONS/0038 item 2 and 0039 item 1). You did not write it. About an hour; small registered calculations on processors with predictions first; no card run. Judge whether section 4d, as written, can be failed by the runs it plans, and whether passing it would mean what it says. (1) The statistic (exceedance fractions of R^NR and of zeta at nu = 3 and 4) and its estimator: bias; the effective number of independent cells (the power estimate E-20261125-115822-29795d6 found about 5.5e5 per box and refuted the lead's own predictions W2 and W3: recompute the correlation volume with an estimator of your own from an existing 128-cell output); whether 256 seeds are too many or too few for the stated detection at nu = 4; the variance of the box-scale modes and of the box mean. (2) The reference: the one-patch delta-N calculation for the 128 band (pilot E-20261125-115707-b845282) and the tension the lead reports (the lattice variant at 0.980 of linear, six standard errors). Is it the right reference for what the box measures (coarse-graining scale, the time of the uniform-field surface, linear against nonlinear zeta)? If the code were wrong in a plausible way (a noise amplitude off by a few per cent, a wrong window, a missing backreaction term), would the test at nu = 3 and 4 see it? State the size of error the test can detect. (3) The criteria on constraint scaling with three amplitudes over its range of e-folds, Richardson in the square of the amplitude (128 against 160 cells), the gauge leg (lapse_kdriver = 2), level 2 as a sensitivity: each needs a number fixed in advance and a model test; name the ones that cannot fail. (4) The lead's statement that R^NR is Gaussian to the precision of one box, so that the comparison rests on zeta: check it on existing output with a reader of your own. (5) The budget (about 14 of 60 card-hours) and the order of the runs. Deliver g3/SCOPE_REVIEW.md: findings ranked (blocking / should change / note), each with its evidence and run id, and a proposed wording where a criterion should change; a verdict line: queue the full set as written, or change these items first. The scope text is changed by the lead, not by you.
